narratives.headline: WAF's 4QCY25 result delivered group production of 112koz in line with pre-released guidance, with a stronger-than-expected Kiaka ramp-up offsetting softer Sanbrado output and group AISC of A$2,401/oz beating forecasts by 6%, closing CY25 at 300koz and leaving WAF well-positioned for a material step-up to ~455koz in CY26.
narratives.exec_summary: West African Resources delivered a solid 4QCY25 result, with group gold production of 112koz — up 21% quarter-on-quarter — largely in line with pre-released guidance and analyst forecasts, capping a full-year CY25 tally of 300.3koz at the lower end of the company's guidance range. A stronger-than-expected performance from the Kiaka operation (62.3koz) offset a softer Sanbrado quarter (49.7koz), while group AISC of A$2,401/oz came in approximately 6% below prior estimates, reflecting the benefit of lower costs at Sanbrado (A$2,152/oz). The balance sheet ended the period in robust shape, with cash of A$584m and bullion on hand of A$177m — a combined liquid position that surged approximately 73% quarter-on-quarter — underscoring the company's rapidly strengthening financial position as Kiaka scales toward full capacity. Overall, the tone of the quarter is constructive: the Kiaka ramp-up is progressing well, recoveries have improved to 92.9%, and the operation is now connected to stable grid power, supporting confidence in the CY26 production outlook of approximately 455koz.
narratives.production: West African Resources delivered group production of 112koz in 4QCY25, up 21% quarter-on-quarter, with the result broadly in line with expectations following a pre-release. Kiaka was the standout performer, contributing 62.3koz on the back of better-than-expected head grades of 1.0g/t (versus the 0.9g/t estimate) and recoveries of 92.9%, demonstrating clear progress in the ramp-up trajectory. Sanbrado, meanwhile, came in below expectations at 49.7koz, though the shortfall was more than offset by Kiaka's outperformance, with the group closing CY25 at 300.3koz — at the lower end of guidance.
narratives.outlook: With Kiaka ramping toward an estimated 245koz contribution in CY26 and group production forecast at ~455koz, WAF is positioned for a material step-change in output and free cash flow generation, supported by a strong net cash and bullion position of A$761m exiting CY25. Key catalysts include continued Kiaka throughput and grade performance as the operation scales toward steady-state, while the primary risks remain cost inflation in Burkina Faso, sovereign and security risk in the Sahel region, and any deterioration in the prevailing gold price.
